title: Transactions 7 to 10 and the summary of the month
summary: A note payable, collecting a receivable, wages and a dividend, then the month's totals in Exhibit 3-2.

chunks.heading: Transaction 7: equipment bought on a promissory note
chunks.explanation_md:
Circle Films buys **another ₹9,000 video camera by signing a nine-month promissory note.** Principal and interest are paid at maturity, with interest charged at a **6% annual rate**.

Like transaction 2, it **receives equipment, so assets increase**. Unlike transaction 2, it **promises to pay cash and interest in nine months** instead of paying cash, so **liabilities increase** (Notes Payable).

Table: Equipment ₹9,000 + ₹9,000 = ₹18,000; Notes Payable ₹0 + ₹9,000 = ₹9,000. Total assets ₹30,750 = Liabilities ₹11,000 + Equity ₹19,750.
chunks.exam_line: Equipment bought on a note: equipment (asset) and notes payable (liability) both rise by ₹9,000.

check_questions.answer: Equipment and notes payable both rise by ₹9,000

chunks.heading: Transaction 8: collecting the open invoice
chunks.explanation_md:
Circle Films **receives ₹3,500 from the customer in payment of the open invoice from transaction 6.**

This is an **exchange of one asset for another**: cash increases while receivables decrease. **There is no change in total assets.**

Table: Cash ₹8,250 + ₹3,500 = ₹11,750; Accounts Receivable ₹3,500 - ₹3,500 = ₹0. Total assets stay at ₹30,750 = Liabilities ₹11,000 + Equity ₹19,750. No new revenue is recorded, because it was recorded in transaction 6.
chunks.exam_line: Collecting a receivable: cash up, receivables down; total assets and equity unchanged.

chunks.heading: Transactions 9 and 10: wages and a dividend
chunks.explanation_md:
**Transaction 9: wages of ₹2,000.** Cash falls by ₹2,000, so assets decrease. Payments are an outflow from operating the business, an **expense**, which reduces equity. Cash ₹11,750 - ₹2,000 = ₹9,750; Retained Earnings ₹4,750 - ₹2,000 = ₹2,750. Total assets ₹28,750 = ₹11,000 + ₹17,750.

**Transaction 10: a ₹1,500 cash dividend** paid to owners at the end of the month. Cash and assets decrease. Payments to owners are **dividends**, which decrease retained earnings, so equity decreases. Cash ₹9,750 - ₹1,500 = ₹8,250; Retained Earnings ₹2,750 - ₹1,500 = ₹1,250. Total assets ₹27,250 = ₹11,000 + ₹16,250.

Both lower cash and retained earnings. The difference: wages are an expense of operating; a dividend is a payment to the owners.

chunks.heading: The summary: Exhibit 3-2
chunks.explanation_md:
Circle Films **started the month with nothing but an idea** and ended with **₹27,250 in assets, ₹11,000 in liabilities and ₹16,250 in equity.**

Three lessons from the exhibit:

- **Changes to the left side of the equation equalled changes to the right side** for every transaction, so the equation was always in balance.
- **Every transaction affected at least two accounts.**
- The combinations were: **two asset accounts** (#2 and #8); **an asset and a liability** (#4 and #7); **an asset and an equity account** (#1, #3, #5, #6, #9 and #10).

Any combination of assets, liabilities and equity can occur as long as the equation stays in balance.

**Closing balances:** Cash ₹8,250; Accounts Receivable ₹0; Supplies ₹1,000; Equipment ₹18,000; Unearned Revenue ₹2,000; Notes Payable ₹9,000; Common Stock ₹15,000; Retained Earnings ₹1,250.
chunks.exam_line: Month end: assets ₹27,250 = liabilities ₹11,000 + equity ₹16,250. Every transaction affects at least two accounts.

questions.stem: Show the effect of transaction 7 (the nine-month promissory note) on the accounting equation.
questions.model_answer_md:
Circle Films buys another **₹9,000 video camera** by signing a nine-month promissory note, with interest at 6% a year.

- Equipment rises from ₹9,000 to ₹18,000.
- Notes Payable rises from ₹0 to ₹9,000, because it promises to pay cash and interest in nine months.

Total assets ₹30,750 = liabilities ₹11,000 + equity ₹19,750.

questions.stem: Compare transaction 2 and transaction 7: both buy equipment. What is the difference in their effects?
questions.model_answer_md:
**Transaction 2:** the camera and memory cards are paid for with ₹10,000 cash. Assets both rise and fall, so total assets and liabilities do not change.

**Transaction 7:** a ₹9,000 camera is bought by signing a promissory note. Equipment rises but no cash is paid; instead **liabilities rise** (Notes Payable ₹9,000), so total assets rise.

In both, equipment increases; the difference is whether cash is given up now or a liability is created.

rubric.point: Transaction 2 is an exchange of assets
Total assets unchanged in 2, up in 7
Cash given up now versus promise to pay

questions.stem: Trace wages (transaction 9) and the dividend (transaction 10) through retained earnings.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Transaction 9, wages of ₹2,000:** cash falls from ₹11,750 to ₹9,750. Payments for operating the business are an expense, so retained earnings fall from ₹4,750 to ₹2,750.

**Transaction 10, dividend of ₹1,500:** cash falls from ₹9,750 to ₹8,250. Payments to owners are dividends, which decrease retained earnings, so retained earnings fall from ₹2,750 to ₹1,250.

Assets end at ₹27,250 = liabilities ₹11,000 + equity ₹16,250.

rubric.point: Wages cash and retained earnings fall by 2,000
Dividend cash and retained earnings fall by 1,500

questions.stem: Which transactions in the Circle Films summary are exchanges between two asset accounts, and which involve an asset and a liability?
questions.model_answer_md:
**Two asset accounts:** transaction 2 (cash for equipment and supplies) and transaction 8 (cash collected, receivable reduced).

**An asset and a liability:** transaction 4 (deposit, unearned revenue) and transaction 7 (equipment on a note payable).

The remaining transactions (#1, #3, #5, #6, #9 and #10) affect an asset and an equity account.

questions.stem: Analyse transactions 7 to 10 of Circle Films on the accounting equation and show the totals after each.
questions.model_answer_md:
Position before transaction 7: Cash ₹8,250, Receivable ₹3,500, Supplies ₹1,000, Equipment ₹9,000; Unearned Revenue ₹2,000; Common Stock ₹15,000, Retained Earnings ₹4,750.

**Transaction 7: ₹9,000 camera on a nine-month note at 6%.** Equipment +₹9,000, Notes Payable +₹9,000. Assets ₹30,750 = Liabilities ₹11,000 + Equity ₹19,750.

**Transaction 8: ₹3,500 collected.** Cash +₹3,500 (₹11,750), Receivable -₹3,500 (₹0). Assets unchanged at ₹30,750.

**Transaction 9: wages ₹2,000.** Cash -₹2,000 (₹9,750), Retained Earnings -₹2,000 (₹2,750). Assets ₹28,750 = ₹11,000 + ₹17,750.

**Transaction 10: dividend ₹1,500.** Cash -₹1,500 (₹8,250), Retained Earnings -₹1,500 (₹1,250). Assets ₹27,250 = ₹11,000 + ₹16,250.

The equation balanced after each transaction.
